ok.description: Indicates whether the request succeeded. Always `true` for successful responses.

match_count.description:
The total number of insights that match the search criteria, across all pages. When the
request carries a cursor, it is the total for the criteria of the original search, not
the number of insights that remain.

return_count.description:
The number of insights that have been returned in the response.
When this number equals the page size, which is the requested `size` capped at 5000,
the response carries a `cursor` and there might be more insights to return.

cursor.description:
The cursor to the next page of insights. Pass it in the `cursor` field of the
next search request. It is omitted when the page has fewer insights than the page
size, which is the requested `size` capped at 5000. For example, a request with a
`size` of 6000 that returns 5000 insights carries a cursor. The cursor is an opaque
value: do not parse it or build one yourself, because its format can change without
notice.

insights.description: The insights that match the search criteria.

@timestamp.description: The time when the insight was raised, in ISO 8601 format (UTC).

tags.description:
The tags of the insight, for example `domain:performance` or `scope:node`.
Tag values keep the casing in which they are defined. The list of tags is
available at https://ela.st/autoops-insights.

message.description: The context and conditions that led to the insight being raised, as plain text.

Insight.description:
An insight. Properties that have no value are omitted from the response instead of
being set to `null`.

title.description: The human-readable title of the insight, as plain text.

actions.description: The recommended actions to troubleshoot the insight, in the order to carry them out.

type.description: The identifier of the action type, in lowercase.

title.description: The human-readable title of the action.

description.description:
A description of the action and its purpose. It can contain HTML markup, such as
`<code>` tags, and it can be empty.

command.description: A command that carries out the action. Omitted when the action has no command.

Severity.description: The severity level of an insight.

id.description:
The ID of the rule that raised the insight, in lowercase. Use it in the `rules` field
of a search request. The list of rule IDs is available at
https://ela.st/autoops-insights.

name.description: The short, human-readable name of the rule.

description.description: The description of the rule and an explanation of its potential impact, as plain text.

name.description: The index name(s). Always an array, even when only a single index is affected.
The node name(s). Always an array, even when only a single node is affected.

id.description: The node ID(s). Always an array, even when only a single node is affected.

tier.description: The data tier of the nodes, for example `hot`, `warm`, or `cold`.

id.description: The ID of the Elasticsearch cluster.

name.description: The name of the Elasticsearch cluster. It can be empty when the cluster has no name.

id.description: The resource ID (deployment ID, project ID, or connected cluster ID).

name.description: The name of the resource. It can be empty when the resource has no name.

id.description: The ID of the organization that owns the resource.
The public ID of the insight, as a UUID.

start.description: The time when the insight was raised, in ISO 8601 format (UTC).

end.description: The time when the insight was closed, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Omitted while the insight is open.

duration.description: The duration of the insight in nanoseconds (`end` minus `start`). Omitted while the insight is open.

updated.description:
The time when AutoOps last updated the insight, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). It equals `start`
when the insight is raised, AutoOps moves it forward each time it confirms that the insight
is still open, and it equals `end` when the insight is closed.

url.description: The URL that returns this insight.

ok.description: Indicates whether the request succeeded. Always `true` for successful responses.
